existing_rule_updates.update: Clarified the adjective's main semantic-predicate role in be + AdjP; added Chapter 6 pp. 526–527 sources and two examples.
Added Chapter 6 p. 527 source support for the absence of adverb predicative function; retained the existing engine scope.
Expanded the modifier category inventory to include prepositions and determinatives, preserving the caveat that not every adverb modifies every category.
Added Chapter 6 p. 527 source support for adjective-to-adverb -ly derivation.
Clarified the single AdjP level and recorded rare direct-NP complement uses of worth and like, with two exception examples and one ordinary PP example.
Clarified the single AdvP level and the qualified generalization that AdvP expansion is broadly a subset of AdjP expansion.

meta.note: No standalone new rule was necessary: the section's applicable grammatical distinctions were already represented by the approved rule base, and its contribution is source-backed refinement and conceptual clarification.

concepts.gloss: The single higher-level syntactic unit headed by an adjective; the phrase may contain modifiers and, where licensed, complements.
The single higher-level syntactic unit headed by an adverb; its possible internal expansions are broadly a subset of those available to AdjPs.
An adjective phrase can function as a clause complement while the adjective supplies the main semantic predicate and be carries tense and subject agreement.
Adjectives almost always denote states, while verbs are commonly used for dynamic situations, although many verbs also denote states.
A rare adjective that takes an NP complement directly; the section names worth and like as examples.
